subject.title: [security] External lifecycle templates can place inherited config credentials on argv

question: Should inherited trusted `external.config` values be treated as sensitive/source-bound when a repository-defined External lifecycle template expands them into argv, steps, or resource names?
rationale: The source path is clear, but the fix can change documented External adapter behavior for non-secret config values that currently flow through argv, so maintainer security and compatibility intent is required before automation should implement it.

options.title: Track config provenance
options.body: Mark trusted or environment-origin `external.config` template values sensitive and require the existing explicit argv/resource-name opt-ins or a non-argv channel when a lower-trust lifecycle references them.

options.title: Accept current behavior
options.body: Treat inherited `external.config` argv expansion as part of repository executable automation and update docs/security text to remove the implied source-bound credential protection for this case.

options.title: Docs-only warning
options.body: Warn operators not to store secrets in `external.config` without changing runtime behavior, which preserves compatibility but leaves the reported source-bound credential flow available.

recommendation.title: Track config provenance
recommendation.body: Mark trusted or environment-origin `external.config` template values sensitive and require the existing explicit argv/resource-name opt-ins or a non-argv channel when a lower-trust lifecycle references them.

likelyOwner.reason: This person is tied to both the External lifecycle implementation and the merged security-boundary policy that maintainers cited for adjacent External behavior.
